producedBy.what: One page, put through the GetLoopLoop Vectorscope's fetch, extract and chunk steps locally, with the product's 26-passage cap, and no embedding step. Grouped by Claude's reading, not by embeddings; groups are a judgement, chunking and the 26-passage cap are the product's exact rules.

howToRead.grouping: Grouped by Claude's reading, not by embeddings; groups are a judgement, chunking and the 26-passage cap are the product's exact rules. The product groups passages by average-link clustering over embedding similarity; here the passages were read and grouped by subject instead, so two runs can group the same page differently. For the embedding-based reading with the map, run the page at https://www.getlooploop.com/vectorscope.
howToRead.unitOfAnalysis: A chunk is one passage as the pipeline split it — roughly 2000 characters, following the page's own headings where it has them. Chunks overlap by about 200 characters, so their lengths sum to more than the page.
howToRead.textHead: Only the first 240 characters of each chunk are included. Across this page that is 6053 of 41850 indexed characters, about 14%, and always the opening of each passage rather than a sample spread through it.
howToRead.keywords: Counted over the page's whole text, not the excerpts below. A term is one word or two: a two-word term is a pair the page writes side by side often enough that the pair is what it is saying, and where it is counted neither of its words is counted separately, so the occurrences still add up to the page. `count` is occurrences; `groups` is how many of the page's groups the term reaches, and `scope` is true when it reaches most of them. A term with `scope` true describes the page; one with it false is a single section's vocabulary — useful, but not a summary. Plurals were folded into the singular where the page uses both. The group counts rest on the grouping above, which is a judgement.
howToRead.groupLabels: `labelSource` says where each name came from. "heading" is the page's own section heading and can be quoted. "keywords" is a computed guess — the group's most distinctive words — and is a hint, not a topic; do not quote it back as what the section is called.
howToRead.cohesion: null: cohesion is the mean cosine between a group's passage embeddings, and no embeddings were computed.
howToRead.selfSimilarity: null: the median cosine between passages needs embeddings, and none were computed.
howToRead.groupFloor: null: there was no similarity cut; the groups are a reading of the passages.
howToRead.duplicateOf: The index of an earlier, non-adjacent chunk this one repeats nearly word for word, as judged by reading — the product judges it from embeddings at cosine 0.94. The chunker's own overlap between neighbours is excluded.
howToRead.projectionExplained: null: there is no projection without vectors.
howToRead.whatCapReachedMeans: The pipeline indexes at most 26 chunks per page. `capReached` true with `charsUnread` above zero means an assistant reading this page never sees that tail.
howToRead.noindex: True when the page asks search engines not to index it. Says nothing about whether an assistant can read it, but it is often unintentional.

cannotAnswer: Sentiment or tone of the page. Only about 14% of the text is here, taken from the opening of each passage — enough to produce a confident-sounding verdict from an unrepresentative sample. If asked, say what the sample supports and that it is a sample.
Anything about competitors, or how this page compares to another. One page was read; no other page was fetched.
Which search or assistant prompts this page ranks or gets cited for. That needs a query inventory and measurement over time, neither of which is in this export.
Whether the page is factually correct, current, or original. Nothing here checked any claim on it.
How the page renders for a browser running JavaScript. This is a plain fetch, which is also what an assistant that does not run JavaScript sees.

How close any two passages are in an embedding space, or whether any assistant has indexed this page. No embeddings were computed, and this is a preview of the machine's view, not a guarantee of what any assistant does with it.
suggestedPrompt: This is a retrieval read-out of one web page. Using it, tell me: (1) what this page is about — lean on `keywords` where `describesWholePage` is true, since those are counted over the full text rather than the excerpts — group by group, naming groups only where labelSource is "heading"; (2) what someone asking an assistant about this subject would find here, and what they would not; (3) what to change first, ordered by how much it would change what an assistant retrieves — cite the chunk indexes or group ids your answer rests on. Where the payload's cannotAnswer list says the data does not support a claim, say so instead of estimating.
